subject.title: fix(discord): bound webhook send body reads

question: Should Discord webhook delivery adopt the same fixed 15-second wall-clock budget as the REST client even though an already-accepted non-idempotent webhook request may still complete remotely after the local abort?
rationale: The code can consistently implement either boundary, but selecting the user-visible timeout and duplicate-delivery tradeoff is an owner policy decision rather than a mechanical correction.

options.title: Adopt the shared 15-second budget
options.body: Accept bounded failure for slow webhook sends, provided the PR adds exact-head runtime proof and the failed required check is resolved or shown unrelated.

options.title: Use a different webhook contract
options.body: Request an owner-defined budget or idempotency/retry strategy if Discord webhooks need different delivery semantics than REST sends.

options.title: Pause this change
options.body: Keep the existing unbounded webhook behavior until the Discord delivery contract and upgrade risk can be decided.

recommendation.title: Adopt the shared 15-second budget
recommendation.body: Accept bounded failure for slow webhook sends, provided the PR adds exact-head runtime proof and the failed required check is resolved or shown unrelated.
